authority.policy: Installed native connectors and plugin-owned MCPs suppress generated direct duplicates. Shared-remote MCPs may be persisted across hosts because they create no local server process. On-demand-local MCPs are removed from host configuration unless lifecyclePolicy.persistedOnDemandLocalMcpIds records a reviewed lightweight exception. The appium-mobile exception may persist its provider registration but never starts the VM or emulators. Skills-only plugins must not declare MCP servers owned by registry/mcps.json. Package-cache presence alone is not activation proof; only observed installed/runtime-owned surfaces are classified as owners.

hostPrivateExtensionPolicy.conflictPolicy: A host-private extension is outside fleet parity unless it claims a canonical capability or MCP identity, creates a duplicate canonical registration in the same host, or violates a machine resource or safety boundary.
hostPrivateExtensionPolicy.runtimePolicy: Host-private child processes may be observed for aggregate resource evidence but are not AgentHub-managed MCP runtime drift and are never terminated by AgentHub.

lifecyclePolicy.hostConfiguredLocalFanoutPolicy: appium-mobile may be registered persistently where no package activation route exists; registration is lightweight and does not start the VM or emulators

onDemandLocalCoverage.why: generatedAt is bumped by this reconciliation, so it would otherwise read as a claim that onDemandLocalMcpIds covers every on-demand-local server in registry/mcps.json as of today. It does not. This block is what keeps the bumped date from overclaiming, and it is the record that the gap was seen rather than missed.

added.appium-mobile: Registered 2026-08-10 with activationMode on-demand-local, owned by capability mobile-device-lab, after the previous generatedAt of 2026-07-31. Straightforward staleness: it is an on-demand-desktop stdio process started by its owning capability, the same shape as chrome-devtools, so this policy governs it on the same terms.

notAdded.chrome-devtools-isolated: Registered 2026-08-06 with activationMode on-demand-local. Not added here because whether it is governed as a separate lifecycle id or as part of its chrome-devtools sibling is a decision about how browser-toolkit exposes the pair, and no host exposure list in this file names it at all -- adding it to the lifecycle list alone would record a governance claim the exposures do not back.
notAdded.repowise-workspace: Registered 2026-08-07 with activationMode on-demand-local but scope global-default and 18 declared hosts, unlike every id currently in this list. localFanoutPolicy says an on-demand-local id is never persisted in host configuration; a global-default server with 18 hosts is the shape that normally IS persisted. Which of the two is correct was not measured against the deployed host configs, and recording it either way without that measurement is the assumption this registry exists to forbid.

onDemandLocalCoverage.nextStep: Measure both against the deployed host configurations, then either add them here or record why each is exempt. Until then this list is complete for what it claims and explicitly incomplete for what it does not.

ownerActionRequired.rationale: An action the owner authorized that AgentHub cannot perform is state, not a footnote. Recorded here it survives the session that discovered it, carries the evidence for why the limit is real, and can be audited later; left in a chat transcript it is indistinguishable from work quietly skipped.
ownerActionRequired.boundary: This list is only for actions AgentHub genuinely cannot perform. It is not a queue, not a backlog, and not somewhere to defer work. tests/Test-OwnerActions.ps1 fails the build on any entry that claims AgentHub could perform the action and has not, so the cheapest way out of this file is to do the work rather than record it.
ownerActionRequired.completionPolicy: An entry stays after completion with completedOn set, because the record of what the owner had to do by hand is the useful part. Never delete an entry to mark it done.

actions.authorization: Owner instruction, verbatim: 'I feel comfortable getting rid of tavily as they have very low allowance and we have alternate liek exa, brave and firecrawl already?' and 'remove Atlassian, Asana, Slack and Figma as well'.
actions.fleetSideEvidence: None of the five is registered in registry/mcps.json, which declares nine servers, and none appears in any host exposure list in this file. The fleet-side removal the owner asked for is done; what remains is outside the fleet.
actions.blockedBy: RESOLVED 2026-08-05. Retained for the record: no authenticated browser surface reached claude.ai account settings from this machine, and entering credentials to obtain one was prohibited. The owner authenticating the session themselves was the route through, and it was available the whole time -- worth remembering next time a limit looks absolute, because 'AgentHub cannot authenticate' was true while 'this can never be done from here' was not.
actions.blockerVerification: Claude in Chrome list_connected_browsers returned an empty array on 2026-08-04 and again on 2026-08-05. The in-app browser carries no claude.ai session, and authenticating one would require entering the owner's credentials, which is prohibited regardless of authorization. Verified twice rather than assumed, because a capability limit asserted without testing was wrong once already in this work.

apiProbe.detail: Probed for a programmatic route before concluding this needs a browser at all. The connector-registry MCP exposes list_connectors and search_mcp_registry but no disconnect or remove operation, so there is no write path even in principle. Both reads returned empty -- including a registry SEARCH for 'atlassian' and 'slack', which cannot legitimately be empty. So the empty connector list is evidence the integration could not enumerate, NOT evidence that zero connectors are installed. Recorded so the next reader does not mistake this for a clean inventory, and does not repeat the probe believing it untried.

actions.ownerStep: claude.ai -> Settings -> Connectors -> select the connector -> Disconnect. Disconnecting also revokes nothing at the provider; see oauth-grant-revocation.

localSurfaceProof.why: The earlier blockers recorded that no route REACHES claude.ai. This records something stronger and more useful: the five connectors are not present on the local surface at all, so there is nothing here to disconnect even in principle. That reframes the entry from 'AgentHub is blocked' to 'AgentHub is complete and the remainder belongs to a different system'.
localSurfaceProof.claudeMcpList: 9 servers: sentry, github, notion, descript, chrome-devtools, context7, exa, firecrawl, linear. None of Tavily, Atlassian, Asana, Slack or Figma appears. This matches registry/mcps.json's declared nine exactly.
localSurfaceProof.claudePluginList: 15 plugins, all enabled, all from claude-plugins-official or agenthub. None of the bundles that carry the five servers (engineering, marketing, small-business, design, litigation-legal, adobe-for-creativity) is installed locally.
localSurfaceProof.conclusion: The bundles are account-level: claude.ai injects them into a session rather than installing them on this machine. `claude plugin disable` cannot act on them because `claude plugin list` cannot see them -- checked, not assumed, because that same CLI turned out to have the answer once before when a limit was asserted without testing it.
localSurfaceProof.browserRoutesRetested: Both retested live on 2026-08-05, not carried forward from the earlier attempt. The in-app browser at claude.ai/settings/connectors redirects to the sign-in page ('Continue with Google / email / SSO'), carrying no session. claude-in-chrome list_connected_browsers returned [] for the third separate time. The only remaining route is entering the owner's credentials, which is prohibited regardless of authorization.

actions.ownerClickPath: claude.ai -> Settings -> Connectors, then Disconnect on each. For a server that arrives via an account-level plugin bundle rather than as a standalone connector, the control is on the bundle, so consult bundleContents in this file first: removing a bundle to drop one server also drops the others listed beside it.

completion.howItUnblocked: The owner signed in to claude.ai in the in-app browser. That single act converted every recorded blocker at once: the blocker was never the settings UI, it was the absence of an authenticated session, and the owner supplying one is not the same as AgentHub entering credentials -- which remained, and remains, prohibited.

completion.verification: Re-read the connector table after the removal. The rows now run Exa -> GitHub Integration with nothing between them, where Figma previously sat. Verified by reading the table back, not by trusting that the dialog closed.
completion.residualNotClaimed: Removing a connector on claude.ai does not revoke the OAuth grant on Figma's side. That is the separate provider-side action tracked in this file and is NOT claimed as done here. A removal here and a revocation there are different acts against different systems, and collapsing them is precisely the kind of overstatement this registry exists to prevent.

actions.action: revoke the OAuth grant for a connector the owner removed
actions.surface: the provider's own account security / connected-applications page
actions.authorization: Owner instruction, verbatim: 'remove Atlassian, Asana, Slack and Figma as well'. A removal whose grant is still live leaves an authorization standing against the owner's account, so the grant is part of what was asked for.

scopeCorrection.was: targets were Linear, Notion and Descript; authorization read 'Follows from the owner's connector reduction: a disconnected connector whose grant is still live remains an outstanding authorization against the owner's account.'
scopeCorrection.why: That sentence is an inference, not an instruction, and every other entry in this file quotes the owner verbatim. The entry manufactured its own authorization and then sat beside genuinely authorized ones, where the difference is invisible. Worse, the inference was false on its facts: the owner never asked for Linear, Notion or Descript to be removed, and claude mcp list on 2026-08-05 shows Linear and Notion CONNECTED and in active use in the same session that was treating their revocation as unfinished work. Acting on this entry would have broken two working integrations to satisfy a completion condition.
scopeCorrection.lesson: An ownerActionRequired entry is a claim that the owner wants something. Deriving one from a related request is how a to-do list grows items nobody asked for -- and an entry that cannot quote its instruction should not be able to look like one that can.

policy.rule: AgentHub does not vendor, fork, mirror, or re-host a third-party plugin. Each host installs it from that host's own official channel and updates it with that host's own command. This block records which channel each host uses and what was last observed there, so a host silently falling behind is detectable; it does not grant AgentHub install authority, which hostPrivateExtensionPolicy withholds for claude and codex.
policy.whyNotAMarketplaceEntry: Adding a third-party plugin to .claude-plugin/marketplace.json would make AgentHub the publisher of code it does not own, pin it to whatever revision AgentHub last copied, and cut the host off from the upstream release stream. The official per-host channel is what keeps it current.
